name: dispatchly
description: Field service dispatch demo with .NET 10, EF Core, React, TypeScript, tests and CI

paragraphs: A field-service dispatch dashboard built from scratch with .NET 10, ASP.NET Core, EF Core, SQL Server support, React, and TypeScript.

Portfolio demo. The public frontend runs in browser preview mode and stores changes in local storage. Run the API locally for live database-backed operations. The backend is not yet a production SaaS: it has no user accounts, tenant isolation, or migrations.

I selected a line-of-business product because current full-stack .NET roles repeatedly ask for C# APIs, relational data, React/TypeScript, testing, and cloud delivery. The key engineering example here is scheduling: the app rejects an assignment when its time interval overlaps another job for the same technician. The current overlap check is suitable for a demo but needs a database-level concurrency strategy before multi-user production use.
features: Create a job, optionally assigning a technician.
Prevent overlapping appointments for the same technician.
Assign unclaimed jobs and advance them through scheduled, in progress, and completed.
Inspect a job's customer, address, priority, and assignment.
